name: Regenerative Agriculture
region: Global (Amazon Basin, West Africa, Southeast Asia, North America, Australia)
summary: Farming systems that actively restore soil health, biodiversity, and water cycles rather than depleting them, drawing on Indigenous land management and modern agroecology.

claims.statement: Terra preta soils demonstrate that pre-Columbian farmers engineered self-renewing fertility lasting millennia
West African agroforestry systems maintain soil carbon and crop yields without synthetic inputs across centuries
Modern regenerative practices (cover cropping, no-till, rotational grazing) measurably increase soil organic matter within 5-10 years

evidence.source: Glaser, Haumaier, Guggenberger & Zech (2001) The Terra Preta phenomenon, Naturwissenschaften 88
Fairhead & Leach (1996) Misreading the African Landscape: Society and Ecology in a Forest-Savanna Mosaic, Cambridge UP
LaCanne & Lundgren (2018) Regenerative agriculture: merging farming and natural resource conservation profitably, PeerJ 6:e4428
Lal (2004) Soil carbon sequestration impacts on global climate change and food security, Science 304(5677)

notes: First resolved cross-link in the graph: terra_preta → regenerative_agriculture → carbon_sequestration. Demonstrates multi-generational lineage tracking.
